name: Generator London
description: Stylish hostel in a converted police station near King's Cross. Social atmosphere with a bar, cafe, and events.
tips: Private rooms available too. Great location near King's Cross and the British Library.

name: Point A Hotel Shoreditch
description: Smart, compact rooms with everything you need in trendy Shoreditch. Modern design, great WiFi, and excellent location.
tips: Rooms are small but perfectly designed. Steps from Shoreditch's best bars and restaurants.

name: hub by Premier Inn Covent Garden
description: Brilliantly located compact hotel right in Covent Garden. Control your room from an app - lights, TV, temperature.
tips: Unbeatable location for West End theatres. Smart tech-enabled rooms. Book early for best rates.

name: The Hoxton Southwark
description: Design-led boutique hotel with a lively lobby, rooftop bar, and excellent on-site dining. Cool, creative atmosphere.
tips: The rooftop restaurant Seabird has stunning views. Walk to Tate Modern, Borough Market, and the South Bank.

name: The Zetter Townhouse Clerkenwell
description: Boutique Georgian townhouse hotel with individually designed rooms full of vintage curiosities. Award-winning cocktail lounge.
tips: The cocktail lounge is one of London's best. Each room is unique. Perfect romantic getaway.

name: citizenM Tower of London
description: High-tech hotel with mood lighting, rain showers, and king-size beds. Stunning views of the Tower of London from the rooftop bar.
tips: The rooftop bar has incredible Tower of London views. Self-check-in kiosks. Great for tech lovers.

name: The Savoy
description: A legendary 5-star hotel on the Strand. Art Deco glamour, impeccable service, and Thames views. London luxury at its finest.
tips: Even if not staying, visit the American Bar for cocktails or book their famous afternoon tea.

name: Claridge's
description: The epitome of London luxury. Art Deco masterpiece in Mayfair with legendary service. The afternoon tea is world-famous.
tips: The Art Deco foyer is worth seeing even if you're not a guest. Afternoon tea here is a bucket-list experience.

name: Shangri-La The Shard
description: London's highest hotel, occupying floors 34-52 of The Shard. Infinity pool with city views. Unforgettable skyline vistas.
tips: The infinity pool on the 52nd floor is London's most spectacular. Bar and lounge on floor 35 open to non-guests.

name: Safestay London Elephant & Castle
description: Modern hostel in a beautifully converted Victorian mansion. Dorms and private rooms with a garden and communal kitchen.
tips: Great budget option with good transport links. The building itself is gorgeous. 10 mins to central London.

name: Wombat's City Hostel London
description: Award-winning hostel near Tower Hill with a large communal kitchen, bar, and friendly atmosphere. Clean and well-run.
tips: One of London's best-rated hostels. The WomBar downstairs is a great place to meet fellow travellers.

name: Clink78 Hostel
description: Hostel in a stunning 200-year-old Victorian courthouse near King's Cross. Unique character with original courtroom features preserved.
tips: The old courtroom is now the common area. Charles Dickens visited this building. ClashBar in the basement is fun.

name: St Christopher's Inn Borough
description: Party hostel right next to Borough Market with Belushi's bar downstairs. Social, lively, and perfectly located for South Bank exploring.
tips: Right next to Borough Market for incredible street food. Belushi's bar has happy hour deals. Great social scene.

name: YHA London Central
description: Modern purpose-built hostel in a great location between Oxford Street and King's Cross. Clean, safe, and excellent facilities.
tips: Best family-friendly hostel in London with private family rooms. Walk to the British Museum in 5 minutes.

name: Selina Camden
description: Trendy co-working and co-living hostel in vibrant Camden. Rooftop terrace, yoga classes, and a creative community vibe.
tips: Great for digital nomads with co-working space. Steps from Camden Market and the live music scene.

name: SoHostel
description: Budget hostel in an unbeatable Soho location. Basic but clean rooms minutes from Oxford Circus, Piccadilly, and Theatreland.
tips: You cannot beat this location for budget accommodation. Soho nightlife, restaurants, and theatres on your doorstep.

name: The Hoxton Shoreditch
description: The original Hoxton hotel that started the brand. Industrial-chic rooms, buzzy lobby, and a restaurant that draws locals and guests alike.
tips: The lobby is always buzzing. Excellent brunch at Hoxton Grill. Heart of the Shoreditch nightlife scene.

name: The Hoxton Holborn
description: Stylish boutique hotel in a grand former office building. Lofty lobby with co-working vibes, cocktail bar, and great restaurant.
tips: Stunning lobby space for working or lounging. Walk to the British Museum, Covent Garden, and the West End.

name: citizenM Shoreditch
description: Trendy tech-forward hotel in the heart of Shoreditch. MoodPad-controlled rooms, art-filled lobby, and 24/7 canteen.
tips: King-size beds and rain showers as standard. The lobby living room is great for hanging out and working.

name: citizenM London South Bank
description: Design-led hotel steps from the Tate Modern and the South Bank cultural strip. Compact but beautifully designed rooms.
tips: Walk to Tate Modern, Shakespeare's Globe, and Borough Market. Great value for this prime cultural location.

name: The Z Hotel Soho
description: Compact, stylish rooms in the heart of Soho with complimentary wine and cheese each evening. Unbeatable West End location.
tips: Free wine and cheese 4-8pm daily is a lovely touch. Rooms are small but smart. Best Soho location.

name: The Z Hotel Piccadilly
description: Chic budget-boutique hotel just off Piccadilly Circus. Small but perfectly formed rooms with premium bedding and free evening wine.
tips: Steps from Piccadilly Circus and Leicester Square. The complimentary evening cheese and wine is a great bonus.

name: Point A Hotel King's Cross
description: Ultra-modern compact hotel with excellent transport links from King's Cross and St Pancras. Smart design maximises small spaces.
tips: Eurostar connection at St Pancras next door. Great value for the location. Power showers and smart TVs.

name: Mama Shelter London Shoreditch
description: Playful, colourful hotel with a vibrant rooftop bar and restaurant. Eclectic interiors, DJ nights, and a fun social atmosphere.
tips: The rooftop is one of east London's best hangouts. Sunday brunch with bottomless drinks is legendary.

name: The Pilgrm
description: Independent boutique hotel in Paddington with curated interiors, a locally sourced restaurant, and a cosy neighbourhood feel.
tips: Heathrow Express from Paddington makes arrival easy. Lovely independent coffee shop downstairs.

name: Qbic London City
description: Eco-friendly design hotel in Whitechapel with modular room pods, a lively bar, and strong sustainability credentials.
tips: Great for eco-conscious travellers. Near Brick Lane for incredible curry and street art. Motilo room pods are fun.

name: The Ritz London
description: Legendary luxury hotel on Piccadilly with Louis XVI-style interiors, world-famous afternoon tea, and impeccable white-glove service.
tips: Afternoon tea here is a London institution - book months ahead. Jacket and tie required in The Ritz Restaurant.

name: Brown's Hotel, a Rocco Forte Hotel
description: London's first ever hotel, opened in 1837. Quintessentially English luxury in Mayfair with Olga Polizzi-designed interiors.
tips: Alexander Graham Bell made the first ever telephone call from here. The English Tea Room is gorgeous.

name: Corinthia London
description: Grand Victorian-era hotel near Trafalgar Square with an extraordinary spa, opulent suites, and world-class dining.
tips: The ESPA Life spa is one of London's most spectacular. Kerridge's Bar & Grill by Tom Kerridge is exceptional.

name: Rosewood London
description: Edwardian Belle Epoque mansion in Holborn transformed into a grand luxury hotel. Stunning courtyard entrance and Scarfes Bar.
tips: Scarfes Bar is one of London's best cocktail bars and open to non-guests. The courtyard entrance is magnificent.

name: The Ned
description: Soho House group's grand hotel in the former Midland Bank HQ. Nine restaurants, a rooftop pool, and stunning 1920s banking hall.
tips: The rooftop pool and terrace have incredible City views. The ground-floor restaurants in the old banking hall are open to all.

name: The Standard London
description: Bold, retro-futuristic hotel in a brutalist 1970s building opposite St Pancras. Rooftop restaurant with panoramic views and a red London bus library.
tips: Decimo on the 10th floor serves incredible Spanish-Mexican food with views. The exterior lift ride is an experience itself.

name: NoMad London
description: New York import in a stunning Grade II-listed Bow Street magistrates' court. Beautifully restored with a soaring atrium restaurant.
tips: The atrium restaurant is jaw-droppingly beautiful. Perfect for theatre-goers - Royal Opera House is next door.

name: Pan Pacific London
description: Ultra-modern luxury hotel in the City with an infinity pool, destination spa, and exceptional dining in a striking skyscraper.
tips: The 18.5m infinity pool is stunning. Straits Kitchen serves excellent Southeast Asian cuisine. Spa is world-class.

name: Bulgari Hotel London
description: Italian opulence meets Knightsbridge luxury. Silver and mahogany interiors, a spectacular spa with 25m pool, and private cinema.
tips: Next door to Harrods. The spa and 25m pool are among London's finest. Sette restaurant serves superb Italian.

name: hub by Premier Inn Westminster
description: Tech-savvy compact hotel in the shadow of Westminster Abbey. App-controlled rooms and a rooftop bar with Parliament views.
tips: Rooftop bar has killer views of Big Ben and the Houses of Parliament. Incredible value for this location.

name: Town Hall Hotel
description: Art Deco former town hall in Bethnal Green transformed into a design-forward boutique hotel with a Michelin-starred restaurant.
tips: Da Terra restaurant has two Michelin stars. The building's Art Deco and Edwardian features are beautifully preserved.

name: Ham Yard Hotel
description: Firmdale Hotels' colourful retreat tucked away in a courtyard off Piccadilly. Rooftop terrace, bowling alley, cinema, and theatre.
tips: There is a bowling alley, rooftop garden, and private cinema in the hotel. Kit Kemp's interiors are extraordinary.

name: The Lanesborough
description: Regency splendour on Hyde Park Corner. Personal butler service, opulent interiors, and Celeste restaurant with a Michelin star.
tips: Every guest gets a personal butler. The Library Bar makes some of London's finest cocktails. Overlooking Hyde Park.

name: One Aldwych
description: Independent luxury hotel in a striking Edwardian building at the gateway to Covent Garden. Chlorine-free pool, modern art, and Eneko restaurant.
tips: The chlorine-free swimming pool is unique among London hotels. Excellent for Covent Garden and West End access.

name: Ace Hotel London Shoreditch
description: Portland-born creative hotel bringing its signature cool to Shoreditch. Vinyl turntables in rooms, gallery space, and Hoi Polloi restaurant.
tips: Rooms have Rega turntables with a curated vinyl selection. Miranda bar in the basement is a local favourite.

name: Great Northern Hotel
description: Beautifully restored Victorian railway hotel right on King's Cross station. Curved corridor of rooms, excellent restaurant, and superb location.
tips: Plum + Spilt Milk restaurant is excellent. Directly connected to King's Cross station. Eurostar at St Pancras next door.

name: South Place Hotel
description: Slick, design-led hotel in the City with rooftop terraces, a secret garden, and two excellent restaurants. Great for business and leisure.
tips: Two rooftop terraces are lovely in summer. Angler restaurant has a Michelin star. Secret garden is a hidden gem.

name: Batty Langley's
description: Whimsical Georgian townhouse hotel in Spitalfields with elaborately themed rooms evoking 18th-century London. Utterly unique.
tips: Each room is themed to a different era. Steps from Brick Lane and Spitalfields Market. A truly one-of-a-kind stay.

name: The Bermondsey Square Hotel
description: Quirky boutique hotel on a lively square in trendy Bermondsey. Vibrant design, a fun cocktail bar, and antiques market on the doorstep.
address: Bermondsey Square, Tower Bridge Rd, London SE1 3UN
tips: Friday morning antiques market on the square. Walk the Bermondsey Beer Mile of craft breweries. Near Tower Bridge.

name: The Mandrake
description: Artful boutique hotel in Fitzrovia with a lush courtyard garden, rooftop terrace, and ever-changing art installations throughout.
tips: The Jurema terrace is magical in the evening. Rotating art installations mean it is different every visit. Serene spa.

name: Artist Residence London
description: Bohemian-chic boutique hotel in Pimlico with just ten individually designed rooms. Cambridge Street Kitchen serves excellent seasonal food.
tips: Only ten rooms so book early. Each room features original artworks. Walk to Tate Britain and Victoria station.

name: Treehouse Hotel London
description: Playful, nature-inspired hotel near Oxford Street with a stunning rooftop bar offering 360-degree London views.
tips: The Nest rooftop has some of the best views in London. Near BBC Broadcasting House and Oxford Street shopping.

name: Lost Property St Paul's London
description: Curios-filled boutique hotel near St Paul's Cathedral themed around London's lost and found. Quirky design with a playful spirit.
tips: Walk to St Paul's Cathedral in two minutes. The lobby cafe is a lovely spot for breakfast. Fun themed design.

name: The Kensington Hotel
description: Elegant Victorian townhouse hotel in the heart of South Kensington. Classic English interiors, a tranquil garden, and easy access to three world-class museums.
tips: Steps from the V&A, Natural History Museum, and Science Museum. The garden is a peaceful retreat. Harrods is a short walk.

name: Travelodge London Central Tower Bridge
description: Reliable budget chain hotel with clean, no-frills rooms in an excellent Tower Bridge location. Great value for money.
tips: Walk to Tower Bridge and the Tower of London. Book well in advance for the best rates. Breakfast is extra but nearby cafes are better value.

name: Premier Inn London Southwark (Tate Modern)
description: Dependable mid-budget hotel right on the South Bank cultural strip. Consistent rooms, hearty breakfast, and unbeatable proximity to the Tate Modern.
tips: One of the best-value locations in London. Borough Market is across the road and Tate Modern is a two-minute walk.

name: Travelodge London Central Marylebone
description: Budget-friendly hotel on a quiet Marylebone street within walking distance of Oxford Street and Regent's Park.
tips: Walk to Regent's Park and Madame Tussauds. Marylebone High Street has excellent independent shops and cafes.

name: ibis London Blackfriars
description: Modern budget hotel in a prime Southwark location near the Thames. Simple, comfortable rooms with a 24-hour bar and snack service.
tips: Surprisingly good location for the price. Walk across Blackfriars Bridge for St Paul's or south to the Tate Modern.

name: Astor Hyde Park Hostel
description: Friendly hostel in a Victorian townhouse near Hyde Park and the museums of South Kensington. Free breakfast and walking tours included.
tips: Free breakfast is a real money-saver. Walk to the Natural History Museum and V&A. Hyde Park is two minutes away.

name: easyHotel South Kensington
description: Ultra-budget micro-rooms in the heart of South Kensington. No frills but spotlessly clean, with everything you need for a short stay.
tips: Rooms are tiny but the location is top-tier. Book the slightly larger rooms if you can. Great for museum visits.

name: The Montague on the Gardens
description: Charming traditional hotel overlooking the private gardens of Bedford Square, right next to the British Museum. Classic English elegance.
tips: Ask for a garden-view room. The terrace overlooking the gardens is heavenly for afternoon tea. British Museum is next door.

name: The Marylebone Hotel
description: Stylish contemporary hotel on Marylebone's prettiest street. Excellent spa, refined dining, and a calm village-like atmosphere.
tips: Marylebone High Street is one of London's loveliest shopping streets. The in-house spa is a real treat.

name: The Bloomsbury Hotel
description: Grand Neo-Georgian hotel designed by Edwin Lutyens in the heart of literary Bloomsbury. Beautiful ballroom and elegant bar.
tips: The Lutyens-designed ballroom is extraordinary. Directly opposite the British Museum. The Coral Room cocktail bar is stunning.

name: Mondrian Shoreditch London
description: Design-forward lifestyle hotel with a rooftop pool, destination restaurant, and curated art programme in the heart of Shoreditch.
tips: The rooftop pool and terrace are a big draw in summer. Christina's restaurant serves excellent modern European food.

name: The Gore London - Starhotels Collezione
description: Eccentric Victorian hotel near the Royal Albert Hall, crammed with over 5,000 prints and antiques. Each room is individually decorated.
tips: Perfect for concert-goers - the Royal Albert Hall is a two-minute walk. Each room is stuffed with fascinating antiques.

name: Premier Inn London County Hall
description: One of London's best-value hotels in a spectacular riverside location. Views of the Thames, Big Ben, and the London Eye from select rooms.
tips: Request a river-view room for incredible Big Ben views. Possibly the best-value location in all of London. Book months ahead.

name: Ruby Lucy Hotel London
description: Trendy lean-luxury hotel near Waterloo with compact, beautifully designed rooms, a vibrant bar, and guitars available to borrow.
tips: Borrow a guitar from reception for your room. Walk to the South Bank, London Eye, and Waterloo station. Great cocktail bar.

name: Hazlitt's
description: Enchanting boutique hotel in three Georgian townhouses in the heart of Soho. Antique-filled rooms with four-poster beds and literary heritage.
tips: Named after essayist William Hazlitt who lived and died here. No two rooms are alike. A secret literary treasure in Soho.

name: The Connaught
description: Understated Mayfair elegance with Michelin-starred Helene Darroze restaurant, award-winning Connaught Bar, and beautifully serene rooms.
tips: The Connaught Bar is regularly voted one of the world's best. The Aman spa in the basement is pure tranquillity.

name: The Berkeley
description: Fashionable Knightsbridge luxury hotel with a rooftop pool, Blue Bar, and the famous Pret-a-Portea fashion-inspired afternoon tea.
tips: The rooftop pool is a London rarity. Pret-a-Portea afternoon tea features pastries inspired by fashion collections.

name: Great Scotland Yard Hotel
description: Luxury hotel in the original Scotland Yard police headquarters near Trafalgar Square. Rich history with modern opulence.
tips: The building was the original Metropolitan Police HQ. Fascinating historical details throughout. Walk to Trafalgar Square and Whitehall.

name: The Londoner
description: Super boutique hotel on Leicester Square with eight underground levels including a screening room, spa, and multiple restaurants.
tips: Eight floors go underground including a private cinema. Right on Leicester Square for theatres and nightlife. The Retreat spa is superb.

name: St. Ermin's Hotel
description: Historic hotel near St James's Park with a stunning ornate lobby, rooftop bee garden, and fascinating connections to British espionage.
tips: MI6 recruited agents in this hotel during WWII. The rooftop bees produce honey used in the restaurant. Incredible ornate lobby.

name: Native Borough Market
description: Apartment-style hotel in a converted warehouse right above Borough Market. Full kitchens, living spaces, and the best food market in London at your feet.
tips: Having a kitchen above Borough Market means you can cook with the finest ingredients in London. Feels like living in the city.

name: Point A Hotel Paddington
description: Smart micro-hotel near Paddington station with well-designed compact rooms, powerful showers, and excellent Heathrow Express access.
tips: Heathrow Express makes this perfect for early flights. Hyde Park is a short walk away. Rooms are small but smartly designed.
